definition: DeepSeek is a generative artificial intelligence chatbot developed by the Chinese company DeepSeek.
details: Released on 20 January 2025, DeepSeek-R1 surpassed ChatGPT as the most downloaded freeware app on the iOS App Store in the United States by 27 January. DeepSeek's success against larger and more established rivals has been described as "upending AI" and initiating "a global AI space race". DeepSeek's compliance with Chinese government censorship policies and its data collection practices have also raised concerns over privacy and information control in the model, prompting regulatory scrutiny in multiple countries. However, it has also been praised for its open weights and infrastructure code, energy efficiency and contributions to open-source artificial intelligence.

explainer.lead: DeepSeek is a generative AI chatbot from the Chinese company DeepSeek, best known for the rapid rise of its R1 release. It matters because it challenged much larger rivals while earning praise for its open weights, infrastructure code and energy efficiency, alongside concerns about censorship and privacy.

tiers.eli5: DeepSeek is like a very quick pen pal that writes answers when you send it a message. Its R1 version became so popular that its iPhone app passed ChatGPT in US freeware downloads just a week after release. People like that some of its building parts are shared openly, but they worry about what information it collects and whether some answers are held back.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer can evaluate DeepSeek-R1 through the chatbot or work with its open weights and infrastructure code. Before deployment, test outputs for censorship-related information limits and review the service's data collection practices against privacy requirements. Regulatory scrutiny in multiple countries makes that review especially important.
tiers.paperLevel: DeepSeek is a generative AI chatbot developed by the Chinese company DeepSeek; DeepSeek-R1 was released on 20 January 2025. Known concerns include compliance with Chinese government censorship policies, which can limit information, and data collection practices that raise privacy questions. Its open weights and infrastructure code are notable contributions to open-source artificial intelligence.

explainer.example: A user opens the DeepSeek app and asks it to explain a topic; the chatbot generates an answer. That interaction also illustrates the two main cautions: censorship compliance may limit information, and data collection may affect the user's privacy.
